heroHeadline: Sheinbaum Defies Washington — Allows Iran's World Cup Team to Stay, Asserting Mexican Sovereignty
heroSubtitle: Mexico's 701-year national arc spans the founding of México-Tenochtitlán (1325), the Spanish Conquest (1521), 300 years of colonial New Spain, the Independence War (1810–1821), the Reform era and French Intervention, the Porfiriato (including Yaqui ethnic cleansing 1899–1908), the Mexican Revolution (1910–1920), seven decades of PRI hegemony, and the democratic transition of 2000. Today, President Claudia Sheinbaum — Mexico's first female president — signs land restitution decrees for the Yaqui people (45,794 hectares returned since 2019), governs amid the CJNG succession crisis (Day 77 since El Mencho's killing), faces the formal USMCA bilateral round in 15 days (May 25, Mexico City), and prepares for the FIFA World Cup opening in 32 days.
footerNote: Comprehensive national intelligence dashboard aggregating Mexico's full historical arc from 1325 to present. Data sourced from INEGI, Banxico, SESNSP, SEDENA, SRE, OHCHR, InSight Crime, and major international outlets.
